situation:
You are the supporter communications manager at HARROW COUNTY FC, a second-division professional soccer club that has played in the same city for forty years. The commercial director (judge) has asked you to recommend what the club tells the ticket holders whose home match was abandoned last Saturday, when a lightning storm settled over the ground and stayed there.

The match was called at halftime and will not be replayed. The club's published inclement weather policy promises a like-for-like exchange into a future home match, not a cash refund, and the league requires the club to post its decision within seven days of an abandoned match. Half the seats sold that night went to households buying their first Harrow County ticket.

The club's own ticketing data says exchange offers hold on to these buyers better than refunds do, measured across four seasons of weather calls. The ticket office staff who took the calls on Sunday say otherwise. They heard first-time attenders who read an exchange as a runaround, and TIDEGATE ATHLETIC, the expansion club that opened across the county two years ago, is selling to those same households.

Offering every ticket holder an exchange into a future home match follows the published policy and the reading the ticketing data supports, and it sends the first-time attenders the ticket office spoke to away with the impression the staff described. Issuing cash refunds to everyone who asks and writing to them individually answers that impression, and it gives back a full home gate in a season the club is already losing seats to TIDEGATE ATHLETIC.

The commercial director (judge) wants your recommendation on what the club offers these ticket holders, how the letter to a first-time attender should differ from the letter to a season ticket holder, and how the club makes its case without waving away what the ticket office heard. The commercial director (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
